In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Ya-Sin

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Ya Sin﴾. The verified view is that it is among the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'a) that occur at the beginnings of surahs. The letter yā' mentioned in it has been mentioned at the opening of Surat Maryam, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Kaf Ha Ya' Ayn Sad﴾ [Maryam: 1]. The letter sīn mentioned in it has been mentioned at the beginning of al-Shu'ara' and al-Qasas, in His saying: ﴿Ta Sin Mim﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 1], and at the beginning of al-Naml, in His saying: ﴿Ta Sin﴾ [al-Naml: 1], and at the beginning of al-Shura, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Ha Mim Ayn Sin Qaf﴾ [al-Shura: 1-2].

We have already presented a complete discussion of the disjointed letters that open surahs at the beginning of Surat Hud.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 2:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the Qur'an, full of wisdom﴾ ﴿Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾. We have already explained that the reason for the emphasis on his being among the messengers is the denial of the disbelievers regarding that, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger"﴾ [al-Ra'd: 43]. This was discussed in Surah al-Baqarah, in the commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿These are the verses of Allah; We recite them to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 252].

Al-Shinqiti on Surah Yasin, verse 6:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾. The particle "mā" in His saying ﴿whose forefathers were not warned﴾ — it has been said that it is negative (nāfiyah), and this is the correct view. It has also been said that it is relative (mawṣūlah), in which case it is the second object of "tundhira" (you warn). And it has been said that it is verbal-masdariyyah (a particle forming a verbal noun with the following verb).

We have already set out the evidence of the verses that it is negative, and that among what indicates this is its ordering, by the particle fa' (so/therefore), before it of His saying after it: ﴿so they are heedless﴾. For their being heedless fits the absence of warning, not warning itself. This is the apparent meaning, together with other verses that indicate it, as we have fully clarified in Surah "Banī Isrā'īl" (Al-Isra), in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ [Al-Isra: 15].

(p-287) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Certainly the word has come into effect against most of them, so they do not believe﴾. The apparent meaning is that "the word" in His saying ﴿the word has come into effect against most of them﴾, and in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them, and the word came into effect against them among nations [that had passed away] before them of jinn and mankind﴾ [Fussilat: 25], and in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Those against whom the word has come into effect will say: Our Lord, these are the ones we misled; we misled them as we ourselves were misled﴾ [al-Qasas: 63], and in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and the word will come into effect against the disbelievers﴾ [Ya-Sin: 70], and in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿so the word of our Lord has come into effect against us: indeed we are to taste [the punishment]﴾ [al-Saffat: 31], and the "word" in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, those against whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 96–97], and in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿They will say: Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect against the disbelievers﴾ [al-Zumar: 71], refers to His saying, exalted is He, ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together﴾ [Hud: 119]. This is as indicated by verses of the Book of Allah, exalted is He, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He, at the end of the surah "Hud": ﴿And they will continue to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy. And for that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾ [Hud: 118–119];

• His saying, exalted is He, in "al-Sajdah": ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾ [al-Sajdah: 13];

• His saying, exalted is He, at the end of "Sad": ﴿He said: The truth, and the truth I say: "I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you from among them, all together."﴾ [Sad: 84–85].

And His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿Certainly the word has come into effect against most of them﴾, indicates that most people are of the people of Hell, as many verses also indicate, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾ [Hud: 17]; ﴿And most of mankind will not be believers, however much you may desire it﴾ [Yusuf: 103]; ﴿And certainly most of the earlier peoples had gone astray before them﴾ [al-Saffat: 71]; ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 174].

We have already discussed this in the surah "al-An'am", in the commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you obey most of those on the earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah﴾ [al-An'am: 116].

(p-288) And we have explained, by the authentic Sunnah (the prophetic tradition), at the beginning of the surah "al-Hajj", that the portion of the Fire out of every thousand is nine hundred and ninety-nine, and that the portion of Paradise from it is one.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks, and they reach to the chins, so they are held up [with their heads raised]﴾ and ﴿We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see﴾.

Al-aghlal (the shackles) is the plural of ghull (a shackle, a yoke), which gathers the hands to the necks. Al-adhqan (the chins) is the plural of dhaqan, which is the meeting point of the two jaws. Al-muqmah, in the form of the passive participle, is one who raises his head. As-sadd, with a fatḥah or a ḍammah on the sīn, is the barrier that blocks the path of reaching what lies behind it.

His saying, fa-aghshaynahum, means: We placed over their eyes a ghishawah (a covering), which is the veil that is over the eye and prevents it from seeing. From the same root is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And over their eyes is a covering﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7], and His saying: ﴿And He has placed over his sight a covering﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 23]. And the saying of the poet, who is al-Harith ibn Khalid ibn al-As:

"I loved you when a covering was over my eye; when it was lifted away, I cut off my soul, blaming it."

The meaning of the noble verse is that these wretched ones, for whom wretchedness had preceded in the knowledge of God, those mentioned in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Certainly the word has been fulfilled upon most of them, so they do not believe﴾, God turned them away from faith with a great turning that prevents it from reaching them. For whoever has a shackle placed on his neck, and the shackle reaches his chin, so that his head remains raised and he cannot lower it, and whoever has a barrier placed in front of him and a barrier behind him, and whoever has a covering placed over his sight, has no means to act, nor to bring benefit to himself, nor to avert harm from himself. Thus, those whom God has made wretched in this condition, good does not reach them.

This meaning indicated by this noble verse, namely that the Exalted turns away the wretched ones, for whom wretchedness had preceded in His knowledge, from the truth, and comes between them and it, has been made clear in many verses:

• Such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness﴾ [al-Kahf: 57],

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿God has sealed over their hearts and over their hearing, and over their sight is a covering﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7],

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you seen one who has taken his desire as his god, and God has sent him astray knowingly, and has sealed over his hearing and his heart, and has placed over his sight a covering?﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 23],

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever God wills to send astray, He makes his breast constricted and tight, as if he were climbing up into the sky﴾ [al-An'am: 125],

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever God sends astray, there is no guide for him﴾ [al-A'raf: 186], (p-289)

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever God wills to test, you cannot avail him anything against God. Those are the ones whose hearts God did not will to purify; for them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 41].

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts, hearing and sight God has sealed, and they are the heedless﴾ [al-Nahl: 108],

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they had no protectors apart from God; the punishment will be doubled for them. They were not able to hear, and they did not see﴾ [Hud: 20],

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whose eyes were under a covering from My reminder, and they were unable to hear﴾ [al-Kahf: 101],

and the verses of like meaning are many.

It has already been stated that this sealing and stamping upon the hearts, and likewise the shackles upon the necks, and the barrier before them and behind them, all these barriers that prevent faith and the arrival of good to the hearts, God placed them upon them only because of their hastening to deny the messengers and their persistence in disbelief. So God punished them for that by obliterating their insight, sealing their hearts, stamping them, and placing a covering over their sight. For it is among the evil consequences of sins that God, the Exalted, punishes their doer for them by his persistence in evil and by the barrier between him and good. God repays him for his disbelief with a fitting recompense.

The verses that indicate this are many:

• Such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Rather, God has stamped upon them because of their disbelief﴾ [al-Nisa': 155], where the bā' is causal. In the verse there is an explicit statement from Him, the Exalted, that the cause of that stamping upon their hearts is their disbelief;

• And such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were stamped﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 3]. It is known that the fā' is one of the particles of causation, meaning: their hearts were stamped because of that disbelief of theirs,

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5],

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sight as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'am: 110],

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so God increased them in disease﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10],

and other verses besides these, as has been previously explained.

These verses indicate that the evil consequence of sins drags its doer into persistence in sins. And it is understood by the opposite implication of this that doing good leads to persistence in doing good, and so it is. As the Exalted said: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad: 17]. And His saying, (p-290) the Exalted: ﴿And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69], and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever believes in God, He guides his heart﴾ [al-Taghabun: 11], and other verses besides these.

Know that the view of whoever among the people of knowledge said that the meaning of His saying, the Exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks﴾, is that what is meant by these shackles are the chains with which they will be punished in the Hereafter, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When the shackles are around their necks and the chains; they will be dragged through the scalding water, then in the Fire they will be burned﴾ [Ghafir: 71-72], is contrary to the verification. Rather, what is meant by placing the shackles upon their necks, and what is mentioned with it in the verse, is their being turned away from faith and guidance in the abode of this world, as we have made clear.

Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs, from 'Asim, read this word as sadda, with a fatḥah in both places. The rest read it with a ḍammah on the sīn. Both readings have one meaning, and they are correct. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You can only warn the one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful in the unseen﴾. Its clarification has already been given, together with its counterparts among the verses, in surah "Fatir", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord in the unseen and establish the prayer﴾ [Fatir: 18].

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-377) In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Surah Ya-Sin

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You can only warn the one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful﴾, the verse.

Its apparent meaning is that the warning is specific to those who benefit from it. Its counterpart is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 45].

Other verses have come that indicate the generality of warning:

• such as His saying: ﴿And you warn thereby a people contentious in dispute﴾ [Maryam: 97],

• and His saying: ﴿That he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [Al-Furqan: 1],

• and His saying: ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire flaming﴾ [al-Layl: 14].

We have already mentioned the way of reconciling these: that warning in reality is general, and it was restricted in some verses to the believers to show that they are the ones who benefit from it, to the exclusion of others, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 55].

He made clear that warning and its absence are equal with respect to the faith of the wretched by His saying: ﴿It is equal for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 6].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forward and their traces, and We have enumerated everything in a clear record (imam mubin).﴾ In this noble verse, may He be exalted, mentions four things:

The first: that He gives life to the dead, confirming this by speaking of Himself in the form of majesty (ta'zim).

The second: that He records what they sent forward (qaddamu) in the abode of this world.

The third: that He records their traces (athar).

The fourth: that He has enumerated everything ﴿in a clear record (imam mubin)﴾, that is, in a manifest and evident book. These four things are clarified in other places.

As for the first of them, which is His giving life to the dead through resurrection (ba'th), it has come in many verses of the Book of Allah, the Exalted,

• such as His saying: ﴿Say: Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected﴾ [al-Taghabun: 7],

• and His saying: ﴿Say: Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed the truth﴾ [Yunus: 53],

• and His saying: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths: Allah will not resurrect those who die. Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him, true﴾ [al-Nahl: 38],

and verses of the like are many.

(p-291) We have already presented these extensively in surah "al-Baqarah" and surah "al-Nahl," in discussing the proofs of resurrection, and we have repeatedly referred back to that.

As for the second of them, which is His recording what they sent forward in the abode of this world, it has come in many verses;

• such as His saying: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 80],

• and His saying: ﴿This is Our Record; it speaks against you with the truth. Indeed, We were having copied down what you used to do﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 29],

• and His saying: ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird (fate) to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find laid open. "Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner."﴾ [al-Isra': 13-14],

• and His saying: ﴿And the Record will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Woe to us! What is this Record that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it"﴾ etc. [al-Kahf: 49],

• and His saying: ﴿Not a word does he utter but that with him is an observer, ready﴾ [Qaf: 18].

We have already presented some discussion of this in surah "al-Kahf."

As for the third of them, which is that their traces are recorded, it has also been mentioned in some verses.

Know that His saying "and their traces" has two well-known interpretations among the scholars.

The first of them: the meaning of "what they sent forward" is what they themselves did in their lives, and the meaning of "their traces" is what they established in Islam of good or evil practice (sunnah), so it is among their traces which are acted upon after them.

The second: the meaning of "their traces" is their steps to the mosques and similar acts of good, and likewise their steps toward evil, as has been established from him ﷺ that he said: "O Banu Salamah, your dwellings are recorded as your traces," meaning: your steps from your homes to his mosque ﷺ.

As for the first interpretation: Allah, may He be exalted, has explicitly stated that they bear the burdens of those whom they misled and whose evil practices they established, as in His saying: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ etc. [al-Nahl: 25], and His saying: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾ [al-Ankabut: 13].

We have clarified this in surah "al-Nahl," in discussing His saying: ﴿and of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ etc. [al-Nahl: 25] (p-292), and we mentioned the hadith of Jarir and Abu Hurayrah in Sahih Muslim in clarifying this.

Among the verses indicating that a person is held accountable for what is done after him of what he established, of guidance or misguidance, is His saying: ﴿Man will be informed on that Day of what he sent forward and kept back﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 13], based on the interpretation that "what he sent forward" means what he himself did, and "kept back" means what was acted upon after him of what he established, of guidance or misguidance; and His saying: ﴿A soul will know what it has sent forward and kept back﴾ [al-Infitar: 5], according to that view.

As for the second interpretation, that the meaning of "their traces" is their steps to the mosques and similar, some verses have come indicating this meaning, such as His saying: ﴿And they do not cross a valley but it is recorded for them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 121], because that necessarily entails that their steps by which they crossed the valley in their campaign be recorded for them.

As for the fourth, His saying: ﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear record (imam mubin)﴾, it may be indicated by the verses showing the second matter, namely the recording of all deeds they sent forward, on the basis that what is meant is specifically deeds.

As for the supposition that it is general, it is indicated by other verses, such as His saying: ﴿And He has encompassed what is with them and has enumerated everything in number﴾ [al-Jinn: 28], and His saying: ﴿We have not neglected in the Book anything﴾ [al-An'am: 38], based on the view that the "Book" means the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), which is the more correct of the two views. And Allah knows best.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "You are only a human being like us, and the Most Merciful has sent down nothing. You are only lying."﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Bani Isra'il (the Children of Israel), in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 94].

His saying in this noble verse, concerning the disbelievers: ﴿And the Most Merciful has sent down nothing; you are only lying﴾, has made clear that they said that in other places as well, such as His saying: ﴿Every time a company is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, "Did no warner come to you?" They say, "Yes, indeed a warner came to us, but we denied him and said, Allah has sent down nothing..."﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Mulk: 8-9]. (p-293) He, exalted, has also made clear that those who denied Allah's sending down of revelation, like these, did not measure Him with His due measure, i.e., they did not magnify Him with His true magnitude. That is in His saying: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure when they said, "Allah has not sent down anything upon any human."﴾ [al-An'am: 91].

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen (tatayyur, considering something an ill omen). If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and a painful punishment from us will surely touch you."﴾ ﴿They said, "Your omen is with you."﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-A'raf, in the discussion of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And if misfortune strikes them, they attribute it to omens from Moses and those with him﴾ [al-A'raf: 131]. We also mentioned some of the discussion of it in Surat al-Naml, in the discussion of His statement: ﴿They said, "We consider you and those with you a bad omen"﴾, the verse [al-Naml: 47].

Allah's statement: ﴿Follow those who do not ask you for any reward, and they are guided.﴾

I have already presented the verses that clarify this, and the rulings connected with them, in Surah Hud, in the discussion of His statement: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for any wealth in return for it. My reward is only from Allah.﴾ [Hud: 29]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And why should I not worship He who created me, and to Him you will be returned?﴾ His saying "fataranī" (created me) means: "khalaqanī" (created me) and "ibtada'anī" (originated me), as its clarification was already given at the beginning of Surat Fatir.

The meaning is: what reason do I have that would prevent me from worshipping He who created me, originated me, and brought me forth from non-existence into existence? And what this noble verse indicates, that the One who creates alone is the One who deserves to be worshipped alone, has been made clear in many verses of the Book of Allah.

We have already presented the clarification of this in Surat al-Furqan, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they have taken, besides Him, deities that create nothing, while they are themselves created﴾ [al-Furqan: 3], and in Surat al-Ra'd, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or have they attributed to Allah partners who created as He creates?﴾ and the verse [al-Ra'd: 16].

(p-294) The interrogative in His statement, "Shall I take besides Him gods, if the Most Merciful intends for me some harm, their intercession will avail me nothing, nor can they rescue me?" (36:23), is for denial (al-inkar, rejection), and it implies negation. That is, I do not worship, besides Allah, any objects of worship, if Allah intends harm for me that they cannot repel from me, and they cannot rescue me from distress.

What this noble verse contains, namely that the objects of worship besides Allah are of no benefit, is made clear in verses of the Book of Allah, such as:

• His statement: "Say: Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intends harm for me, can they remove His harm? Or if He intends mercy for me, can they withhold His mercy? Say: Allah is sufficient for me; in Him put their trust the trusting." (39:38)

• His statement: "Say: Call upon those you claim besides Him; they have no power to remove the harm from you or to change it." (17:56)

• His statement: "Say: Call upon those you claim besides Allah; they do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth." (10:18)

• His statement: "They say, 'These are our intercessors with Allah.' Say: Do you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth? Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him." (10:18)

• His statement: "And do not invoke, besides Allah, that which neither benefits you nor harms you; for if you do, then you would be among the wrongdoers." (10:106)

Verses of this kind are many and well known.

As for His statement in this noble verse, "their intercession will avail me nothing," it means that there is in fact no intercession for them at all, so that it could avail anything. This sort of construction is a well-known Arabic usage. From it is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*"Upon a faint track, whose landmark one cannot be guided by, when the Nabatean wind lashed it, it rumbled."*

His saying "whose landmark one cannot be guided by" means that there is no landmark at all by which one could be guided. And the saying of another:

*"Its terrors do not frighten the hare, and you do not see the lizard retreating into its burrow there."*

That is, there is no hare in it for its terrors to frighten, and no lizard in it that would "retreat" (yanjahir), i.e., take a burrow (juhr) for itself.

This meaning is the one known among the logicians (al-mantiqiyyun), in their saying: "The negative proposition does not imply the existence of the subject," as its clarification has already preceded.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Alas for the servants! No messenger comes to them but they mock him.﴾ (p-295) He, majestic and exalted, makes clear that no messenger comes to the servants but they mock him, not content merely with denying him, but combining mockery with denial.

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿no messenger comes to them﴾ is an explicit text on the nations' denial of all the messengers, because it is established in the principles (usul al-fiqh) that when an indefinite noun appears in the context of negation and min is prefixed to it, it is an explicit text on the generality of the negation, as is well known in its proper place.

This generality indicated by this noble verse is clarified in other verses, and in some verses one nation is excluded from the ruling of this generality by a connected specifier (mukhassis muttasil), namely the exception (istithna').

Among the verses clarifying this generality is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send a warner into any town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in that with which you have been sent."﴾ [Saba': 34]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And similarly, We did not send before you a warner into any town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps."﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 23]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send into any town a prophet but We seized its people with adversity and hardship...﴾ to His saying: ﴿So We seized them suddenly while they perceived not.﴾ [al-A'raf: 94-95].

We have already presented the discussion of this in the surah "Qad aflaha al-mu'minun" (Surah al-Mu'minun), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Every time there came to a nation its messenger, they denied him...﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 44], and we presented a portion of the discussion of it in the surah "al-An'am", in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We placed in every town its greatest criminals...﴾ [al-An'am: 123].

As for the nation excluded from this generality, it is the people of Yunus (Jonah), and the verse that explains this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Why was there not a town which believed so its faith would benefit it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time.﴾ And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more. So they believed, and We gave them enjoyment for a time.﴾ [as-Saffat: 147-148].

"Al-hasrah" (regret) is the most intense remorse. It is in the accusative because it is a vocative (munada) governing the genitive following it, so it resembles the construct vocative (munada mudaf).

The meaning: "O regret upon the servants! Come, for mockery of the messengers is the greatest cause for your presence."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a sign for them is the dead earth﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Will they not then be thankful?﴾

(p-296) We have already mentioned that the revival of the earth mentioned in this verse is a decisive proof of the resurrection (al-ba'th), in surah al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And sent down water from the sky and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 22]. And in surah al-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sent down water from the sky, from which is drink, and from which are trees upon which you pasture [your herds]﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Nahl: 10], and in other places. And in the places mentioned we have explained the remaining proofs of resurrection after death.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 41:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾ ﴿and We created for them of its like that which they ride﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who subjected the sea, that you may eat from it tender meat﴾ [an-Nahl: 14], and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 46:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And no sign comes to them from among the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it.﴾ In this noble verse, may He be exalted and high, rebukes the disbelievers for their turning away from the signs of Allah.

This meaning contained in this verse also comes in other verses of the Book of Allah:

• Like His saying, may He be exalted, at the beginning of Surah "al-An'am": ﴿And no sign comes to them from among the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it﴾ ﴿Certainly they have denied the truth when it came to them﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-An'am: 4-5],

• And His saying, may He be exalted, at the end of "Yusuf": ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾ [Yusuf: 105],

• And His saying: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split﴾ ﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, "Continuous magic."﴾ [al-Qamar: 1-2],

• And His saying: ﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember﴾ ﴿And when they see a sign, they mock﴾ [al-Saffat: 13-14].

The root of i'rad (turning away, al-I'rad) is derived from al-'Urd (the side), which is the side; because the one who turns away from a thing turns it with the side of his neck, averting from it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and behold, from the graves they will hasten to their Lord.﴾ In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentions the final blast. The Ṣūr (the Horn) is a horn of light into which the angel will blow the blast of resurrection, which is the final blast. When he blows it, all the people of the graves will rise from their graves, alive, for reckoning and recompense.

As for His words, ﴿from the graves﴾: al-ajdāth is the plural of jadath (with two fatḥahs), which means the grave. As for His words, yansilūn (﴿they hasten﴾), it means they hurry in walking from the graves to the place of gathering (al-maḥshar). This is like Allah's saying: ﴿On the Day they will come forth from the graves swiftly, as if they were rushing to a goal post﴾ [al-Ma'ārij: 43]; and His saying: ﴿On the Day the earth will split asunder from them, hastening﴾ [Qāf: 44] and so on; and like His saying: ﴿They will come out of the graves as if they were scattered locusts, hastening toward the caller﴾ [al-Qamar: 7]. His words, muhṭi'īna ilā al-dā'ī (﴿hastening toward the caller﴾), mean hurrying with necks outstretched, according to the most well-known of the two interpretations. From the usage of nasala in the sense of "hastened" is Allah's saying: ﴿until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they swarm down from every slope﴾ [al-Anbiyā': 96], and the verse of Labīd:

*The wolf's swift gait, when he drew near at evening, and the night grew cold upon him, so he hastened (fa-nasal).*

What this noble verse includes, that the people of the graves will rise alive at the second blast, has been clarified in many verses of the Book of Allah, the Exalted:

• Like His saying: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾ [al-Zumar: 68];

• And His saying: ﴿It will be but one shout, and behold, they will all be brought before Us﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 53]. This shout is the second blast;

• Like His saying: ﴿On the Day they hear the Shout in truth. That is the Day of Coming Forth﴾ [Qāf: 42], meaning the coming forth from the graves.

• And His saying: ﴿It will be but one blast, and behold, they will be upon the open ground﴾ [al-Nāzi'āt: 13–14],

The zajrah is the second blast. As for al-sāhirah, it means the surface of the earth and the wide desert, and from this is the saying of Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī:

*They walk upon the sāhirah, whose surface and whose expanse are like the dark cloaks of a gloomy night.*

And the saying of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays:

*And a sāhirah where the mirage covers its regions like a veil; I came to it, wrapped in a veil.*

And:

• Like His saying: ﴿But it will be only one blast, and behold, they will be looking on﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 19];

• And His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command. Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, behold, you will come forth﴾ [al-Rūm: 25]. This call is by the second blast.

• And His saying: ﴿On the Day He calls you, and you will respond with His praise﴾ [al-Isrā': 52],

and other verses besides these.

(p-298) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will say, "Woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place? This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers told the truth."﴾ We have already discussed this in surah "al-Rum," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, "You have remained, according to the Book of Allah, until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the Day of Resurrection."﴾ [al-Rum: 56], and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 60:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And that you should worship Me; this is a straight path.﴾ We have already presented, at length, the verses that clarify this in surah "al-Kahf," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He does not make anyone a partner in His command﴾ [al-Kahf: 26], and we clarified therein the distinction between man-made systems (al-nuzum al-wad'iyyah). And in surah "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright﴾ [al-Isra': 9].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 62:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he had certainly led astray from among you a great multitude (jibillan kathiran). Did you not then reason?﴾

His saying "jibillan kathiran" means a great creation (khalqan kathiran), like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And fear Him who created you and the former generations (al-jibillah al-awwalin)﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 184]. What this noble verse includes, that Satan led astray a great multitude of the children of Adam, has been mentioned in other places, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them all, [and say], "O company of jinn, you have taken much of mankind"﴾ [al-An'am: 128], meaning: you, O devils, have taken much of mankind into misguidance. And Iblis said: ﴿"If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize [control of] his descendants, except a few."﴾ [al-Isra': 62]. And Allah, may He be exalted, has explained that this assumption he made about them, that he would mislead them all except a few, he confirmed against them; and that is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them, so they followed him, except for a group of believers﴾ [Saba': 20], as its clarification has already passed.

Nafi' and 'Asim read this word as jibillan, with a kasrah on the jim and the ba' and a shaddah on the lam. Ibn Kathir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it as jubulan, with a dammah on the jim and the ba' and a light lam. Abu 'Amr and Ibn 'Amir read it as jubslan... [note: correct reading below]

Corrected final sentence: Abu 'Amr and Ibn 'Amir read it as jublan, with a dammah on the jim, a sukun on the ba', and a light lam. All the readings have one meaning, namely: a great creation.

(p-299) His statement, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿And their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify to what they used to earn.﴾ The testimony of some of the disbelievers' body parts against them on the Day of Resurrection, which He mentions here, is explained in more detail in other places. For example, His saying in Surat "al-Nur": ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them as to what they used to do.﴾ [al-Nur: 24], and His saying in "Fussilat": ﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing, their sights and their skins will testify against them as to what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah has given us speech, [He] who gives speech to everything."﴾ [Ghafir: 20–21]. We have already discussed this in Surat "al-Nisa'", in the discussion of His saying: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾ [al-Nisa': 42].

There we explained that this verse of "Ya-Sin" clarifies how the verses are reconciled, such as His saying about them: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾ [al-Nisa': 42], together with His saying about them: ﴿Then their response will be only that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾ [al-An'am: 23], and similar verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 68:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whomever We grant long life, We reverse him in creation. Then will they not reason?﴾.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We reverse him in creation﴾, meaning: We turn him around within it, so that We create him contrary to how We created him before. That is because We created him in weakness of body, empty of reason and knowledge. Then We made him grow and move from state to state, and rise from rank to rank, until he reaches his full strength (ashuddah), completes his power, and comes to reason and know what is for him and what is against him. Then, when he reaches the end, We reverse him in creation, so that he diminishes until he returns to a state resembling the state of a child in the weakness of his body, the scarcity of his reason, and his emptiness of knowledge. The root meaning of al-tankis (reversal) is making the top of a thing its bottom.

This meaning which this noble verse indicates has been made clear in other places:

• As in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is Allah who created you in weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair﴾ [al-Rum: 54], to the end of the verse,

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature. Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ [al-Tin: 4-5], according to one of the two interpretations,

• And His saying in "al-Hajj": ﴿And among you is he who is returned to the most abject age so that he knows, after knowledge, nothing﴾ [al-Hajj: 5],

• And His saying in "al-Nahl": ﴿And among you is he who is returned to the most abject age so that he knows, after knowledge, nothing﴾ [al-Nahl: 70],

• And His saying in surah "al-Mu'min": ﴿Then [He brings you out as infants], then that you may reach your maturity, and then that you may become elders﴾ [Ghafir: 67].

(p-300)

We have already discussed this in surah "al-Nahl". Asim and Hamzah read this letter as nunakkisuhu, with a damma on the first nun, a fatha on the second, and a shaddah on the kaf with kasra, from al-tankis (the intensive form). The rest read it with a fatha on the first nun, a sukun on the second, and a damma on the kaf, lightened, being the imperfect of the bare form nakasahu; both have one meaning. Nafi' and Ibn Dhakwan, from Ibn 'Amir, read: afala ta'qilun with the ta' of address. The rest read: afala ya'qilun, with the ya' of the third person.

The Words of Allah, "And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him" (Surah Ya-Sin 36:69). We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah ash-Shu'ara' (The Poets), in the discussion of His words, "And the poets - the erring follow them" (Surah ash-Shu'ara' 26:224), and we mentioned the rulings related to this there.

Allah's statement: ﴿That he may warn whoever is alive and that the word may be justified against the disbelievers.﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "An-Naml," in the discussion of His statement: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ [An-Naml: 80] and the verse that follows it. And in Surah "Fatir," in the discussion of His statement: ﴿And the living and the dead are not alike﴾ [Fatir: 22].

Allah says: ﴿Have they not seen that We created man from a drop of semen, and then he is an open adversary?﴾

We have already presented the verses clarifying this in Surah "An-Nahl" (The Bee), in the discussion of His saying: ﴿He created man from a drop of semen, and then he is an open adversary﴾ [An-Nahl: 4].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 78:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his own creation﴾, up to His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And He is the Creator, the All-Knowing﴾. We have already explained the verses that clarify this in Surat "al-Baqarah" and "an-Nahl", together with the demonstration of proofs for the Resurrection.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "An-Nahl", in the discussion of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [An-Nahl: 40]. There we explained that the verses mentioned do not contradict the position of the People of the Sunnah (Ahl as-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah) that the term "thing" (shay') is applied to what exists, not to what does not exist. We have also already presented the two recitations (qira'atan) and their justification (tawjih) regarding His words, ﴿Be, and it is﴾, there.
